title: Applied ML Evals Integrated Playbook: Eval Harness, Prompt Sets and Benchmarks, Model Onboarding, Guardrails, Quantization, and Regression Triage
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood's applied ML evaluation practices across the eval harness, canonical prompt sets and benchmarks, model onboarding requirements, quality guardrails, quantization profiling, and regression triage. It is intended as the single-source-of-truth for model owners, applied ML engineers, and release managers when bringing a model into serving or when diagnosing quality regressions in production.

Scope and goals
- Provide a repeatable eval and onboarding workflow that minimizes release risk and enables measurable quality and cost trade-offs.
- Ensure regressions are detected by automated tests and triaged within SLO windows.
- Standardize quantization profiles and test coverage so model performance is predictable across Dedicated and Hosted runtimes.

Owners and contacts
- Primary owner: Applied ML Platform (eng team) — contact: applied-ml-oncall@redwood.example.com
- Secondary owners: Serving Runtime, Observability, and SRE teams (see related pages).

1) Eval harness: architecture and CI integration

Purpose: Provide deterministic, reproducible evaluations for functional, safety, and performance metrics. The eval harness is the canonical runner for all pre- and post-deploy tests.

Components
- Runner: Python-based job that executes prompt sets, collects model outputs, computes metrics, and writes results to S3 + eval DB.
- Metric exporters: standardized JSON/ndjson format with fields: run_id, model_id, prompt_set_id, metric_name, metric_value, seed, environment.
- CI hooks: GitHub Actions jobs that run smoke and full-suite evaluations on PRs and release tags.
- Dashboard: per-model dashboards in Redwood Console showing trendlines and alert triggers.

CI configuration (example)
1. PR smoke: run 10% sample of prompt sets, functional tests only, target runtime < 10m.
2. Nightly full-suite: run all benchmark suites, compute metrics, and publish.
3. Release gate: full-suite plus quantized variants and latency/throughput profiling.

Sample CLI commands
- Run local harness: python -m eval_harness.run --model_id model-x --prompt_set prompts/tech-support.json --out results/model-x-run.json
- Submit to cluster: ./ci/submit_eval.sh --run_id release-2028-12 --suite full

SLOs for the eval harness
- Regression detection sensitivity: detect >= 2% absolute drop in primary metric on critical prompt sets with 95% confidence.
- Test coverage: each production model must have at least 3 critical prompt sets (safety, correctness, domain-specific) and 5 generalization prompt sets.

2) Prompt sets and benchmarks: conventions and catalog

Naming and metadata conventions
- Filenames: {domain}-{intent}-{version}.json (e.g., legal-summary-primary-v1.json).
- Each prompt set must include: id, version, domain, labels (safety/correctness/latency), sample_size, seed, and metric_mapping.
- Tagging: prompt sets are tagged as critical|recommended|optional. Critical prompt sets are used in release gates.

Benchmarking buckets
- Functional correctness: task-specific metrics (ROUGE, BLEU, F1 where applicable).
- Safety: toxicity, refusal rate, PII redaction checks.
- Alignment/regression: metric delta vs. baseline model.
- Latency/cost: p50/p95 latency and tokens-per-second measurements on standard sequence lengths: seq128, seq512, seq2048.

Metric thresholds (example)
- Functional: primary metric (task-specific) must be within -1.5% of baseline for minor releases, within -3.0% for major releases unless approved by product.
- Safety: refusal rate <= baseline + 0.5 percentage points. Toxicity score must not increase by > 0.2 (normalized scale).

3) Model onboarding guide: required artifacts and acceptance criteria

Onboarding checklist (must be attached to onboarding PR):
- Model artifact: exact model weights, architecture, tokenizer, and reproducible load script.
- Benchmarks: eval harness results for unquantized and quantized variants (full-suite).
- Performance profile: latencies (p50/p95) and throughput at seq128/512/2048, memory usage, and peak GPU memory.
- Cost estimate: tokens-per-second and projected unit cost using Redwood Optimize baseline.
- Safety review: auto-scan results (PII detector, toxicity, refusal), and manual review notes if flagged.
- Rollout recommendation: canary percentage, canary duration, fallback model id.

Acceptance criteria (minimum)
- Functional primary metric within thresholds defined in prompt sets (see section 2).
- Latency targets: p95 <= 200ms (seq128), p95 <= 450ms (seq512) on Dedicated n1-standard inference config; if above, require performance mitigations (quantization or kernel tuning).
- Memory and stability: model must not exceed 90% of target GPU memory at max batch 8 for serving.
- Quantization-ready: quantization profile validated (see section 5).

4) Quality guardrails: runtime checks and automated mitigations

Runtime monitors (implemented in serving runtime + Console):
- Output scoring: per-request quality score (ensemble of perplexity delta from baseline, token-level safety flags, classifier-based correctness signal).
- Hallucination heuristics: intrinsic factuality checks for knowledge-intensive prompts. If hallucination score > threshold, escalate to fallback or response with citation request.
- Safety pipeline: blocklist matching, token-level toxicity classifier (threshold: 0.7), PII redaction warnings.
- Latency and resource alarms: if p95 latency rises above SLA + 25% for > 5 minutes, automatic routing to fallback model/region.

Automated mitigations
1. Soft-fallback: attempt a cheaper quantized variant of the same model for up to 30s of degraded performance.
2. Hard-fallback: switch to baseline vetted model after canary fails or severe safety alarm.
3. Rate-limit: applied per-customer route when degraded quality is detected to preserve capacity for critical flows.

5) Quantization profiles and validation

Profile types supported
- q8_compat: 8-bit symmetric, minimal accuracy drop, supported on all GPU types.
- q4_hyper: 4-bit hybrid (per-channel), higher speedups, recommended for generation workloads where quality regression is acceptable within thresholds.
- fp16: half-precision baseline for throughput-sensitive workloads.

Profile template (example)
- name: q4_hyper_default
- bits: 4
- per_channel: true
- ops_excluded: [softmax, layernorm]
- calibration_samples: 2048
- expected_throughput_gain: ~2.8x vs fp16 (seq512, batch=8)

Validation steps
1. Calibration: run calibration with sample set (calibration_samples).
2. Functional regression: run full eval suite and compare to unquantized baseline; flag if primary metric delta worse than thresholds.
3. Performance profiling: measure p50/p95 latencies on standard infra permutations (Dedicated small, Dedicated large, Hosted).
4. Memory regression: confirm peak memory < 90% of target GPU memory.

Quantization rollout strategy
- Start with q8_compat for initial validation. If metrics pass, progress to q4_hyper in a canary pool (5% traffic) with enhanced monitoring for 48 hours.

6) Regression triage playbook: detection to resolution

Purpose: Standardize the human-in-the-loop steps after an automated regression alert. This playbook is used by on-call applied-ml engineers and product owners.

Severity matrix
- Sev 1: Major production regression where primary metric drops >= 5% on critical prompt sets or safety violation confirmed in >1 customer.
- Sev 2: Noticeable regression (2%-5%) or latency SLO breaches affecting a subset of customers.
- Sev 3: Minor metric drift <2% or non-critical prompt set failures.

Triage procedure (numbered steps)
1. Acknowledge alert (on-call) within 30 minutes.
2. Reproduce: run eval harness against the failing commit/model variant. Capture run_id and artifacts.
3. Correlate: check recent releases, model rollouts, quantization events, and infra changes in the last 24-72 hours.
4. Impact assessment: identify impacted customers, routes, and traffic percentage.
5. Mitigation: enact soft-fallback or route-block as defined in quality guardrails.
6. RCA owner assignment: assign an engineer and product owner with a 24-hour remediation SLA for Sev1, 72 hours for Sev2.
7. Fix validation: verify candidate fix with full eval harness and performance profiling in a staging environment.
8. Rollout plan: staged rollout with canary and rollback plan; update postmortem and tracking ticket.

Playbook notes and escalation contacts
- If regression correlates with quantization, revert to last known-good quantization profile and re-run calibration.
- Escalate to Serving Runtime lead if kernel or scheduling changes are suspected.

Postmortem and metrics capture
- For Sev1 incidents, a postmortem must be published within 5 business days and include: timeline, root cause, impact (customers & revenue estimate if known), remediation plan, and follow-up actions assigned.
- Attach eval harness run artifacts, console dashboards, and raw logs to the postmortem.

Appendix: example JSON schema snippets and config tables

Prompt set metadata example (JSON)
{
  "id": "support-clarity-critical-v1",
  "version": "v1",
  "domain": "support",
  "labels": ["critical", "correctness"],
  "sample_size": "200",
  "seed": "20280304",
  "metric_mapping": "{\"primary\":\"accuracy\",\"secondary\":\"latency\"}"
}

Quantization config table (plain text)
- q8_compat: bits=8, per_channel=false, excluded_ops=[layernorm], expected_gain=1.6x
- q4_hyper_default: bits=4, per_channel=true, excluded_ops=[softmax,layernorm], expected_gain=2.8x

Acceptance checklist template (for onboarding PRs)
- [ ] Model artifact and load script attached
- [ ] Full eval harness results (unquantized) attached
- [ ] Quantized variants evaluated and attached
- [ ] Latency p50/p95 report attached for seq128/512/2048
- [ ] Safety scan results attached and reviewed
- [ ] Rollout recommendation and fallback model identified

If you have questions about applicability to a specific model or release, contact the Applied ML Platform on-call or open a ticket in the Applied ML board.
